title: An integral quasi-coherent algebra on a qcqs scheme is a directed colimit of finite (and finitely presented) quasi-coherent algebras
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra* is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]; it is *finite* (resp. *integral*, resp. *of finite presentation*) if for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ the $R$-algebra $\mathcal A(U)$ is finite, i.e. finitely generated as an $R$-module (resp. integral, i.e. every element is a root of a monic polynomial over $R$; resp. of finite presentation, i.e. isomorphic to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$). Let $\mathcal A$ be an integral quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. Then (1) $\mathcal A$ is the directed colimit of its finite quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebras (these form a directed set under inclusion, and the inclusions induce an isomorphism from their colimit to $\mathcal A$); and (2) there exist a directed set $I$, a system $(\mathcal A_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ over $I$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras each of which is finite and of finite presentation, and $\mathcal O_X$-algebra maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$ with $\varphi_{i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_i$, which induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (colimit in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, equivalently of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras). The maps $\varphi_i$ need not be injective.

proof.text: Integrality descends along subalgebra inclusions, whose affine section maps are injective. RingHom.IsIntegral.to_finite identifies finite type and finite subalgebras. The order isomorphism of these two subtypes transports the given finite-type subalgebra colimit, its directedness and its inclusion legs.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof; Tag 086N for eventual finiteness

proof.text: Choose a directed finitely presented module approximation F of the underlying module of A. Use the constructed symmetric algebra sheaves and their unique extension property to define their transition maps and compatible maps to A. The affine comparison and the symmetric algebra finite-presentation theorem make every S_i finitely presented, hence finite type.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof; Tag 086N for eventual finiteness

proof.text: Take the quasi-coherent kernels J_i of S_i to A and choose directed finitely presented module approximations E_ik. Cocone compatibility carries each kernel into each later kernel. Apply the directed-pairs theorem to obtain a directed quotient diagram Q and quotient maps q. Its universal property gives compatible maps Q to A. Compare Q with the generated-ideal quotient, using the two universal properties to construct inverse maps, to obtain affine surjectivity and the kernel span of the image of E_ik. These ideals are finitely generated: the section module E_ik(U) is finite, its linear image is finitely generated, and extending its scalar span to S_i(U) preserves finite generation. Quotients of finitely presented rings by these finitely generated ideals are finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof; Tag 086N for eventual finiteness

proof.text: Form the quasi-coherent algebra colimit of Q and its comparison to A. On an affine open the cocone is a ring colimit. For surjectivity represent an A section in F_i and use its degree-one symmetric algebra section in any quotient in that row. For injectivity represent a colimit section in Q_ik and lift it to S_i. Vanishing in A puts that lift in J_i. Represent the kernel section in some E_ikprime, choose a common later row index, and use the quotient kernel to show the representative vanishes there, hence in the colimit. The affine basis criterion makes the comparison an isomorphism. This directly proves the colimit property without separate row-colimit or iterated-colimit theorems.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof; Tag 086N for eventual finiteness

proof.text: The ring quotient S_i(U)/ker(psi_i(U)) embeds in A(U), so it is integral and finite type, hence finite. Apply eventual finiteness to J_i and E_ik and transport finiteness across the affine quotient isomorphism to obtain bounds k0(i). Pairs above these bounds form a nonempty directed cofinal subtype: increase the second coordinate of any pair, and do the same after taking an upper bound of two pairs. The final inclusion preserves the colimit. Lift the restricted quasi-coherent diagram to the full quasi-coherent subcategory, proving the finite, finitely presented approximation.

lean.statement: theorem integral_algebra_directed_colimit_finite (X : Scheme.{v}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (A : QuasiCoherentAlgebra X) (hA : A.obj.IsIntegral) : (Nonempty A.FiniteSubalgebras ∧ IsDirected A.FiniteSubalgebras (· ≤ ·) ∧ ∃ (c : Cocone A.finiteSubalgebraDiagram) (e : c.pt ≅ A.obj), (∀ B : A.FiniteSubalgebras, c.ι.app B ≫ e.hom = B.val.arrow) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c)) ∧ (∃ (I : Type v) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (F : I ⥤ QuasiCoherentAlgebra X) (c : Cocone (F ⋙ (X.IsQuasiCoherentAlgebra).ι)) (e : c.pt ≅ A.obj), (∀ i : I, (F.obj i).obj.IsFinite ∧ (F.obj i).obj.IsFinitePresentation) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c))
